hypothesis.title: A crash the ghost trigger released is not withheld by the partial-fan-out defer coin: the coin is still drawn, its withhold is ignored for released crashes
hypothesis.description: Nested cell inside the merged release cell (1<<4) by its own salt, half of it (about 0.23 of runs), crossing 1<<28 and the stranded-key cell; bit ghostReleaseDeferExempt = 1<<30 (the retired restartAfterPeerSettle row; a queued candidate lists a claim on it - if that candidate is admitted in the same round, the next untagged retired row). Mechanism: in schedule_runnable (core/scheduler.rs) the crash_defer_mask loop draws rng.random::<f64>() < partial_fanout_crash_bias on the FaultPriority stream for every pending crash whose victim has in_flight != 1 and withholds it for the step. On this cell the draw is kept exactly as is (the stream stays in step with the untreated half) but the withhold bit is not set when state.ghost_release.released_mask has the crash's node bit - the crash a firing released and not yet applied. Counted as crash_place.ghost_release.defer_coin.exempted (withholds overridden) and defer_coin.examined (coin reads on released crashes). Nothing else changes: the step hold, the phase stage on anchored runs, the forced victim and the apply census are the parent's. No config field.
hypothesis.rationale: The release sets the hold to step + 1, but the crash then passes two more admission stages the release was never composed with. The first is the partial-fan-out defer coin: general_vr.json sets partial_fanout_crash_bias 0.5, and the cache reads crash_anchor.timing_bias_withheld 129.7M of 259.5M examined - every pending crash whose victim's in_flight is not exactly 1 is withheld with probability one half per step. The fired in-flight census says released crashes are almost never at in_flight 1: bucket_0 7.6 percent, bucket_1 16.9 percent, bucket_2 16.9 percent, bucket_3plus 58.7 percent (treated cell, seed 1000), so 83 percent of released crashes are coin-subject each step until applied; a fair coin puts one in eight of them past three steps by the coin alone before any scheduling competition. That is a large part of the gap between the release's aim (the next step) and its landing (fired crashes applied within three steps 0.72 on the unanchored stratum). A released crash's victim is, by construction, the peer that has just reacted to a stranded record with its reaction sends in flight - exactly the state the defer coin was written to seek (a crash at a point where a peer is uninformed of the node's last action), so the coin is redundant there and only delays. Holds only shorten; nothing is drawn or skipped.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: A composition rule between two generic stages of the same scheduler: a crash admitted by an event-keyed release should not be re-deferred by a state-keyed coin whose purpose the release already met. Names no protocol term, keeps every random stream in step (the coin is drawn and ignored), never lengthens a hold, and on protocols where the trigger never fires it is a no-op.

crossingHypotheses.title: On the anchored stratum a ghost-released crash's phase wait reads the Early condition on the ghost node's reaction segment whatever arm was drawn: released once that segment has issued a send and none is delivered, else at the phase window
crossingHypotheses.description: Nested cell inside the merged release cell (1<<4) by its own salt, half of it (about 0.23 of runs; the mechanism acts only on the anchored half of that, bit 1<<9, and is byte-identical to the parent on unanchored runs); bit ghostReleasePhaseEarlyOnGhost = 1<<29 (the retired pairOrderGhostOnly row; a queued candidate lists a claim on it - if admitted in the same round, the next untagged retired row). Mechanism: in crash_hold_mask (core/scheduler.rs), after the step hold has passed, a crash whose node bit is in state.ghost_release.released_mask reads its fan-out on state.ghost_release.ghost_node instead of phase_read_node, and crash_phase::RunAnchor::hold_read_on takes a new force_arm: Option<CrashPhaseArm> argument: the Pending slot still draws its arm on the CrashPhase stream (so the stream stays in step with the parent half and the arm counters keep meaning), but the settle is evaluated with CrashPhaseArm::Early when force_arm is Some, and the deadline (armed_at + WINDOW = 96 steps, min the reserve) is unchanged. Counted as crash_place.ghost_release.phase.overridden with the drawn arm (stock_to_early, mid_to_early, early_read_on_ghost) and the outcome (released_on_condition, expired). Release_all, release_one, the forced victim, the learner and the apply census are reused unchanged. No config field.
crossingHypotheses.rationale: 82 percent of fired crashes are applied on the anchored stratum (87,286 of 105,843 on the treated cell, seed 1000), and there the released crash first passes the phase stage: the slot draws Early, Mid or Stock with equal odds at the first offer past the hold. Stock is immediate. Early - the victim's segment issued at least one send and none is delivered - is the exact state of the ghost node one step after it reacted to a stranded record, so it releases at once when read on the ghost node, but the stage reads it on the plan victim (phase_read_node) unless the retarget ranking moves the crash, and the plan victim's segment is unrelated to the reaction. Mid - at least one of the segment's sends delivered - is the opposite of what the release wants: it waits until part of the reaction has landed, and on the oracle path every send of the reacting peer's segment must still be undelivered at its crash (deliver_svc_2_to_0 is ordered after w2, deliver_svc_2_to_1 and deliver_dvc_2_to_1 after deliver_rec_2_to_1). The counters show the cost: fired crashes applied within three steps 0.46 on the anchored stratum against 0.72 unanchored; crash_phase.mid.wait_steps_sum / mid.armed = 24 steps mean wait, early 23, and early's condition is met on 336,265 of 383,626 arms while the phase-landing counters show 280,256 evaluations on another node with 16,277 mismatches at apply. Reading Early on the ghost node removes Mid's contradictory wait (a third of anchored released crashes) and makes the Early read land where the reaction is; it lengthens only the Stock third on the bucket_0 firings (7.6 percent of fired crashes, whose ghost node issued no send), bounded by the 96-step window, which is the parent's own bound.
crossingHypotheses.generalityArgument: A composition rule between two generic stages: a crash released by a reaction-keyed trigger waits, if at all, for the reacting node's own fan-out to be issued and undelivered - the condition the phase stage already defines as Early - rather than for a drawn phase of an unrelated node. Names nothing of the protocol, keeps the CrashPhase stream in step, is bounded by the existing window, and is a no-op on unanchored runs and on protocols where the trigger never fires.

crossingHypotheses.title: The ghost-triggered release fires only on an acted entry whose record belongs to the restarted node's stranded fan-out: the sends its last pre-crash handler segment issued; other dead-incarnation entries neither fire nor disarm the trigger
crossingHypotheses.description: Nested cell inside the merged release cell (bit 1<<4) by its own salt, half of it (about 0.23 of runs), crossing the single cell (1<<28); bit ghostReleaseStrandedKey = 1<<26 (the retired originAlternate row, released by the superseded crash-holds-for-restarted-peer-delivery-window per the iteration-80 admission record; if that row is taken in the same round, the next untagged retired row). Mechanism: in core/scheduler.rs crash_node, BEFORE the existing note_handler_entry(node, HandlerTrigger::None) call overwrites floor, capture the crashed node's last segment into two new SendLedger fields (core/state.rs): stranded_floor = floor and stranded_end = issued (an empty range when the last handler issued nothing). The delivery site already has r.send_ordinal (it feeds pair_order::classify_entry); pass it into note_ghost_release_entry. On this cell the firing condition gains one clause: stranded_floor <= send_ordinal < stranded_end on the origin's ledger. An acted dead-incarnation entry from the origin that fails the clause returns before release_all/release_one and leaves the trigger armed (counted as crash_place.ghost_release.stranded.skipped_entries); the first entry that passes fires exactly as the parent does (release_all on the release-all half, release_one on the single half). Expiry, the learned p75 bound, the learner, RunState, the apply census and the forced-victim path are reused unchanged from ghost_release.rs. Ordinals are monotone across restarts (issued is never reset), so the captured range names the latest crash's segment only. No config field.
buildsOn: pair_order send_ordinal plumbing at the delivery site
crossingHypotheses.rationale: The merged trigger fires on ANY acted entry from the restarted node's dead incarnation (note_ghost_release_entry checks only sent_at != incarnation, acted, origin match, step > restart_step). The oracle's label 4 is the first delivery of a record from the first-crashed node's stranded fan-out - the sends its last handler issued right before label 3 - and label 5 is that peer's crash. A dead-incarnation record from an EARLIER segment of the same node (an acknowledgement or reply still in flight from before the fan-out) acts at a peer, fires the trigger, and releases the held crash before the fan-out record has reached the peer the path needs; the fresh cache shows this too-early landing as depth>=4 0.962/0.968 and depth>=5 0.933/0.945 treated over untreated (my unmatched aggregation of the merged tree's cache; the session's matched read was 0.955). crash_node resets floor to issued at the crash (state.note_handler_entry(node, None)), so nothing on the tree currently remembers which records were the stranded segment; capturing floor and issued one line earlier gives an exact, ordinal-based key. Verified counters (seed 1000 chunk of the fresh cache): armed 232,094, fired 100,609 (0.433 of armed), expired 116,879, released crashes 105,843, lag p50/p75/p90 31/71/151; fired crashes applied within 3 steps 0.72 unanchored and 0.46 anchored; on-ghost-node 0.87 pooled. The share of firings on non-stranded records is not exported; messages held/crossing per crash average 2.7 (crash_recovery.crossing_deliveries 4.38M over 1.65M crashes) against a last-segment fan-out of about 1-2 records, so I expect 30-50 percent of the parent's firings to be on earlier-segment records and this cell to skip them.
crossingHypotheses.generalityArgument: Stated on generic classes only: a node crashed while the sends of its last handler segment were undelivered; one of those sends later changes a live peer's state; that peer is crashed at the next step. It names no handler, message, role or timer label, uses ordinals the ledger already numbers, moves no hold later than the untreated target, draws nothing, and on protocols where the stranded segment never acts the trigger expires and the crash keeps its target - the parent's behaviour.

crossingHypotheses.redTeam: The key is 'the last handler segment before the crash', and floor is reset at EVERY handler entry (state.rs:1154-1163): if the crashed node took any delivery or timer between issuing its fan-out and crashing, the fan-out sits in an earlier segment, the key never matches the path's record, the trigger expires and the crash keeps its drawn target, so the cell loses the parent's gain on exactly those runs. That is guaranteed not to happen only on the anchored Early third (the first crash lands with the current segment's sends all undelivered); on Stock, Mid and unanchored runs it happens whenever the scheduler interleaves one entry at the node. The share of firings on earlier-segment records (the proposer's 30-50 percent) is not exported and the 2.7 crossing deliveries per crash figure counts all crossings, not the pre-fan-out ones. The key does not touch the other half of the too-early loss: the fan-out's sibling record acting first at the peer the DAG keeps up (label 4's sibling is ordered after label 10) still fires. Releases later or never, never earlier: on the skipped runs the cell is the untreated posture, so the depth8 read is a mix of the parent's gain and a partial reversion, and the depth5 recovery may be small.

reviewSummary: Fifteen candidates judged blind against the merged tree (spur 12b7582), the fresh cache 63a21f95fdfb (median 2,517 runs per second), the pool, the oracle DAG and the source. The four new candidates and the two queued siblings are one family nested in the merged release cell (1<<4). Source checks: (1) crash_node sets aside only records addressed to the crashed node (r.node == node_id) and its own outbound in-flight records stay in the network queue - verified, so a stranded fan-out is deliverable after the restart; (2) crash_node calls note_handler_entry(node, None) before touching the queues, that call sets floor = issued and recent = 0, and issued is never reset, so capturing floor and issued one line earlier yields the last pre-crash segment's ordinal range and r.send_ordinal is in hand at the delivery site - verified; (3) the defer coin is drawn for every pending crash with in_flight != 1 whatever its hold and crash_block_mask = defer | hold, so a released crash is re-withheld at 0.5 per step; withheld 129,691,724 of 259,456,919 examined - verified; (4) the phase stage reads on phase_read_node, which is the plan victim unless the retarget ranking moves the read; since 93 percent of fired crashes are on retarget runs and 88 percent of those land on the ghost node, the read already follows the ghost node on most firings - the Early-on-ghost cell's material change is forcing Early over the drawn Mid (a 24-step wait that contradicts labels 5-9) and Stock, not the read node; (5) on the single cell release_one's ranking case runs inside note_ghost_release_entry BEFORE note_ghost_delivery writes v's ghost mark, so the ranking sees only an earlier mark at v and the forced case carries the load (16,261 forced against 5,696 via ranking) - a latent flaw for the implementer to note, not a candidate's claim; (6) the sizePct bands of the new cells are the share of all graded runs carrying the bit (about 0.23) and every band is against the release-without-variant half; the frozen primaries are rewritten as nested contrasts co-bit matched on 1<<9, 1<<19, 1<<28 and the session bits, with the treated-over-untreated read reported beside them. Family order: the defer-coin exemption for released crashes stands first (net 7: one mask test, shortens only, stream in step, verified census; widest population, both strata); the Early-on-ghost phase read (net 6, the sharpened form of the kept-unbuilt early-only ablation, applied to the released crash where the iteration-35 judge said the arm matters) and the stranded-fan-out key (net 6, the only candidate aimed at the depth5 loss, releases later or never) are built with it as crossing cells on their own salts. Bits: 1<<30 ghostReleaseDeferExempt, 1<<29 ghostReleasePhaseEarlyOnGhost, 1<<26 ghostReleaseStrandedKey, all renamed from the retired restartAfterPeerSettle, pairOrderGhostOnly and originAlternate rows in VARIANT_BITS. The at-send cell is closed by its own gate (bucket_0 0.076 and 0.079 against 0.15) and the crash-holds window entry is retired as superseded by the merge; both rejected. The phase-exempt dose (1<<25) waits nested in the Early-on-ghost cell; the condition-released defer exemption (1<<16) waits behind the released-crash exemption; the reply-wait cell moves to 1<<17; the stall repeat moves to 1<<27 and leads the next session; pctPromote, stalled parents and the post-release cap wait on rows freed by closures. Contrast cleanliness: the three session cells change composition, not run length (shorten only; shorten Mid and bound-lengthen Stock bucket_0; release later or never) with every random stream in step; the stall repeat lengthens runs and is graded cross-binary as frozen. Checkable claims found false: the stalled-parents supply (267,533 of 757,560, 35 percent, not 352,842 or half - flagged last round and uncorrected); the replay-arm-set description's 61 percent unfaithful (fresh fidelity 0.55/0.52); the run-local counters' 'fresh baseline' totals 1,468,752,468 / 594,420,962 (this cache: 1,318,696,023 / 559,259,809; the identities hold). Stale but same-shape figures on the stall repeat, post-release cap, PCT timer count, condition-released exemption and reply-wait entries are named in their verifiedClaims.
